title: Authentication and sessions: no login rate limit, the cookie is marked Secure only when NODE_ENV=production (which nothing sets), sessions cannot be revoked, WebSocket sessions are never re-checked after the 24 h expiry, and the length pre-check leaks the key length by timing

evidence.note: loginHandler: unlimited attempts; a failure only logs warn (:56) and answers 401 naming the env var (:57)
apiKey.length !== expected.length returns before timingSafeEqual, so a wrong-length guess answers measurably faster than a right-length one (the "key-length leak" of research J1/J2)

only src/api/middleware/auth.ts:64: nothing in the repo sets NODE_ENV, so the session cookie is never Secure and is sent over plain http to the bot port in the documented remote mode (DASHBOARD_HOST=0.0.0.0)
routes: health, login, the protected /api tree; there is no logout and no way to revoke a session other than its 24 h expiry or a bot restart (sessions is an in-memory Map, auth.ts:17)
the WebSocket validates the cookie once at upgrade; the open socket keeps receiving every broadcast after the session expires (SESSION_TTL_MS is imported at :9 and never used)

sibling_sites_checked: All auth code paths: auth.ts loginHandler, validateSession (:83-93), authMiddleware (:101-110) and the cleanup timer (:21-30); routes/auth.ts (login mount only); ws/handler.ts (cookie parsing :18-29, validation :54). Every /api route sits behind authMiddleware (server.ts:162); /health is deliberately public (AUD-API-010). The login compare itself is constant-time for equal lengths (timingSafeEqual) and a session id is a v4 UUID (auth.ts:61), correct. A key with non-ASCII characters can make the byte lengths differ while the UTF-16 lengths match, so timingSafeEqual throws and the login answers 500 instead of 401 (express 5 catches it; cosmetic). The DNS-rebinding path that makes the missing rate limit reachable from a web page is AUD-API-005.
severity_rationale: S3 EXPOSURE: each item weakens who can drive the money controls only in combination with something else (a guessable key, a network observer in remote mode, a stolen browser); with the default loopback bind and a random key of 16+ characters (enforced by preflight) none of them alone gives control.
recommendation: Add per-IP and global login backoff; set Secure from the actual scheme (or always when DASHBOARD_HOST is not loopback) instead of NODE_ENV; add a logout that deletes the server-side session; close WebSockets whose session has expired (timer or per-broadcast check); compare fixed-length digests (HMAC of both values) so length is not observable. Card API-03 (behaviour change for remote access). Phase 29.

sub_claims.claim: no login rate limit or lockout
cookie Secure depends on NODE_ENV, which nothing sets
evidence: git grep -n NODE_ENV at the base SHA

sub_claims.claim: no logout or server-side session revocation
WebSocket sessions are not re-checked after expiry
